# Pods review at #346

Reviewed exact head `7b2cc29be26a9ea5cbf32ed63b677775c8946474`,
read-only, one reviewer/one round under amended C34.
Verdict: block, commit `1867b18bf4fb934cf988ba68329b7b537f74008b`,
`reviewer/outputs/2026-11/25-verdict-pr-346-7b2cc29.dd.json`.
The author fixes and the prime range-diffs; no second reviewer/round.

## Findings worth remembering

- B346-R1-01: a child first-turn secret refusal does not protect the parent's
  pod parameter/log commit. Validate the whole persistent payload before
  writing, including unused parameters, no-start and later set.
- B346-R1-02: serializing writes is insufficient when each caller reads and
  constructs the replacement before acquiring the writer lock. Concurrent
  successful sets lost one value. Build a read-modify-write under the existing
  serialized closure, as the directory writer does for its own records.
- B346-R1-03: a one-shot canary subscriber exits after initial settlement.
  The advertised later confirm command only publishes an unconsumed event;
  a degraded seat stays stranded. Test the printed repair, not just the
  initial transition.
- B346-R1-04: initial template resolution is caller-relative; later reads
  were repo-relative. The normalized response source was not the persisted
  source. Test from a nested cwd, not only the repo root.
- B346-R1-05: add checked duplicate membership only within its destination,
  silently putting one live seat in two pods. Membership scope affects down
  and subject truth; reconcile the warn-only packet with req-01's refusal
  wording without recording ambiguous ownership.
- B346-R1-06: late work-folder changed the parameter row but not the creation
  metadata down reads. One source of current operational parameters avoids
  this split; subject has the same divergence.
- B346-R1-07: deliverable write-back to a role held by a degraded member
  bypassed the own-dispatch brake. Role addressing does not change the
  destination's membership or who owns the dispatch.
- B346-R1-08: plain CLI rendering expected warning objects while mutating
  verbs returned strings, displayed failed closes as started, and omitted
  promised first turns. Test the actual ordinary CLI view as well as JSON.

The private dispatch test passed with the real set skip and a direct message,
then failed when only that skip was disabled: the mutant was killed.
The existing suite had no equivalent end-to-end assertion.

## Evidence and limits

Exact production-head baseline through shared-build: pod unit 9, history unit 3,
pod HTTP 10, memory-turn HTTP 33, spawn-site sensor 6 all passed; macOS
daemon/CLI/core all-target clippy passed. The close suite proves the successful
memory turn/stop, recycled-PID and cold checks that the pod down integration
fixture only exercises as a refusal. Nine focused daemon probes gave one pass
and eight reproduced failures; two CLI probes failed.

All modifications were confined to private exact-head archives. Niceness 19,
four jobs, shared-build lock and 25 GiB disk floor were preserved. Real-tmux
pij-tmux tests were excluded. No dependencies were installed or symlinked.
Local quick checks were non-green because TS tools were absent/incompatible;
CI and the author's full 17-stage checks receipt at the exact head were green.

The tail reader seeks and caps at 256 KiB. Explicit transcript IDs cannot
contain slash, backslash or dot-dot. Explicit template paths may follow links:
that is the declared path contract, not a C33 same-user isolation defect.
Spawns parent to the resolved caller; role IDs, not type prose, carry authority.
No new migration/dependency source or added home-path/email/private-key marker.

Cost: no new recurring launch/poll path; the canary does have an event-consumer
loop and a single 15-minute deadline, with no down/shutdown-owned task handle.
Bounded tasks can outlive the pod until settlement; do not call that “no timer.”
Up includes existing role-assign commits per slot as well as the pod commits;
down adds one counted git status read plus existing close work.
Live total stayed 1015 over 20 seconds, but the head was undeployed, so req-09
still owes its operation-specific after-deploy receipts. Workstream s02's
complete state and related checked/shipped claims need reconciliation.

## Harness retrospective

magicWand: one read-only exact-head review recipe that creates a private archive,
selects the shared target, runs focused proofs, captures sanitized evidence,
and kills the degraded-dispatch mutant before cleaning only its recorded paths.

difficulties:
- degrading / proof gap: a green suite missed normal-use state loss, repair,
  secret persistence and ordinary CLI output. Fixes should carry these focused
  regression tests, not another broad inventory or review round.
- degrading / tooling: dependency-free review trees cannot supply local TS
  proof; the quick-check error envelope stores its results under error.details,
  not the success data shape. Read the actual envelope and label CI/author
  evidence separately from reviewer executions.
- annoying / discovery: no review procedure exists among the nine listed;
  `pij verdict` is unsupported, while `pij output verdict --head --answers`
  is the working writer.

Disposition: lessons preserved here and in the verdict. An additional review
recipe is only a proposal subject to C35, not authorized new implementation.
The private observation buffer and temporary artifacts are cleaned after this
note is committed; the detached worktree remains unchanged.
